Conformed
kŏn-fôrmd´
v. (made like in form; shaped to a pattern — rendering Greek summorphos and suschematizo)
Latin conformare, to shape together, from con- (with) and forma (form). To be conformed is to take the shape of the mould one lies in.

Biblical Definition

Conformed appears at the two poles of the Christian life, and the two verses must be read together. The first is God's eternal purpose: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren” (Rom 8:29). The end for which the elect were chosen is not bare escape from wrath but a definite shape — the image of Christ, and Christ set forth as the elder brother of a great family all bearing His likeness. The second is the present command: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind” (Rom 12:2). The same root, opposite direction. A man is always being shaped by something. The world presses continually toward its own form, and the pressure works on the outside — habits, speech, appetites, assumptions absorbed without argument. The remedy Paul names is not withdrawal but renewal, and it begins in the mind. Note carefully which conformity is passive and which is commanded. No man conforms himself to Christ's image; that is God's predestinating work, and it is certain. But the command not to be conformed to the world is addressed to the believer's will, and it must be obeyed daily. Sovereign purpose and present duty stand side by side in one epistle and neither weakens the other.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines conform as to make like in form or manner; to bring into harmony or agreement with; and conformed as made to resemble, or brought to correspond with a pattern.

expand to see more

CONFOR'MED, pp. Made to resemble; reduced to a likeness of.

CONFOR'M, v.t. To make like, in external appearance; to reduce to a like shape or form with something else.

2. To bring into harmony or correspondence; as, to conform our lives to the precepts of the gospel.

CONFOR'M, v.i. To comply with, or yield to; to live or act according to a rule or pattern.

Key Scripture

Romans 8:29 — "For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren."

Romans 12:2 — "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

1 Peter 1:14 — "As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance:"

2 Corinthians 3:18 — "But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord."

Modern Corruption

Conformity to the world is reframed as cultural relevance, and the mind — the very place the renewal is commanded to begin — is treated as neutral ground.

expand to see more

The most successful conformity is the kind nobody notices, and the church has repeatedly adopted the world's form while believing itself to be merely translating the message. Paul locates the danger precisely: be not conformed to this world, and then, before any list of practices, he names the battlefield — the renewing of your mind. Conformity is not first a matter of what a Christian does but of what he assumes without examining: what counts as success, what makes a person valuable, what shame is for, what freedom means. These are absorbed by immersion, not by argument, which is why a man can hold orthodox doctrine and still be thoroughly conformed.

Romans 8:29 is also flattened when conformity to Christ's image is reduced to moral improvement. The verse says God predestinated it, so it will happen; and it says the goal is that Christ “might be the firstborn among many brethren,” so the goal is His glory in a family that resembles Him, not the individual's self-actualization. Second Corinthians 3:18 shows the means — beholding, and being changed from glory to glory by the Spirit. The believer is not told to sculpt himself; he is told where to look. What a man beholds, he comes to resemble, and that is as true of the world's images as of Christ's glory.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek summorphos (G4832), jointly formed, conformed to — Romans 8:29, Philippians 3:21; suschematizo (G4964), to fashion after a pattern — Romans 12:2, 1 Peter 1:14.

expand to see more

Greek summorphos (G4832) — jointly formed, similar in form; Romans 8:29 of the image of the Son, Philippians 3:21 of the body of His glory.

Greek suschematizo (G4964) — to conform to a scheme or outward fashion; Romans 12:2 and 1 Peter 1:14 only, both of the world's mould.

Greek metamorphoo (G3339) — to be transformed, the opposite motion in Romans 12:2; the same verb used of the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:2).

Greek anakainosis (G342) — renewing; Romans 12:2 and Titus 3:5, the Spirit's work in the mind.

The two Greek words differ: schema is the outward fashion that changes, morphe the settled form — the world gives a fashion, Christ gives a form.

Usage

"“Predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son” — the certain end of election."

"“Be not conformed to this world” — the daily duty, addressed to the will."

"“Changed into the same image” — a man comes to resemble what he beholds."
